beats.say: You hear whispers of a secret agreement between Austria-Hungary and Italy, signed in secret at the Villa Gherardo.
The pact promised Italy territorial gains in Dalmatia if it stayed neutral, but the Allies intercepted the telegram.
When the treaty leaked, public outrage in Rome forced Mussolini's predecessor to back the war, igniting the Italian front.
Meanwhile, Serbian commanders learned of the deal and launched a desperate offensive at the Drina River, buying months for the Allies.
German General von Falkenhayn used the chaos to shift troops from Verdun to the Eastern Front, altering the battle's outcome.
The hidden treaty reshaped alliances, delayed peace talks, and added a layer of betrayal that still haunts Balkan politics.
